angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 447,335 km at 174.30 pc = 0.03 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.7373 +/- 0.0199 mas (same row, RUWE 1.04): 174.30 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.643 +/- 0.031 solar radii from Thygesen et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-54 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..155T/abstract): 447,335 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.615 +/- 0.031 solar masses from Thygesen et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-54 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..155T/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3990 +/- 300 K from Thygesen et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-54 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..155T/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Thygesen et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-54 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..155T/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-54.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.611, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
